Matched difference-in-differences for merger recipients

Source: R/models.R
merger_did.Rd

Long-difference estimates, from t-2 to t+post, of the change in each outcome for merger recipients against their matched controls, for each design in did_designs(). Each treated unit and its k closest controls form a set; models have set fixed effects, control weights of 1/k, and standard errors clustered by set and organization.

Usage

merger_did(
  data,
  k = 5L,
  spec = "margin",
  gap = 0L,
  keep = ~OTHER == FALSE,
  post = 2L,
  designs = did_designs(),
  outcomes = names(did_outcomes()),
  het = NULL,
  label = "base"
)

did_breakouts(data, by = did_breakout_vars(), ...)

did_sensitivity(data, variants = did_variants(), ...)

Arguments

data

A build_model_data() object.

k

Controls per treated unit.

spec

Matching specification: "margin" or "equity" (the names of health in build_match_data()).

gap

Largest calendar-year gap between a recipient and its controls (with a gap above 0, the models add tax-year fixed effects).

keep

A one-sided formula (or quoted expression or string), evaluated in data$units, that selects the treated units (e.g. ~ OTHER == FALSE & YEAR <= 2021L), or NULL for all.

post

Last event year of the long difference.

designs

Designs to run, from did_designs().

outcomes

Outcome codes, from names(did_outcomes()).

het

Unit-level variables to interact with treatment (see did_breakouts()).

label

Value of the variant column.

by

Breakout variables, from did_breakout_vars().

...

Further arguments to merger_did().

variants

A named list of argument lists, as from did_variants().

Value

A data.table: variant, design, outcome, spec ("pooled" or the breakout variable), term, estimate, se, p, n_obs, n_sets. Log outcomes are log points; ratios and shares are proportions.

Functions

  • did_breakouts(): Breakouts: the treatment effect within each level of each variable in by (one model per variable), alongside the pooled estimate.

  • did_sensitivity(): Sensitivity: merger_did() once per variant, with the variant's name in variant.
